Forensic voice comparison scores

Source: R/data.R
forensic_comparison.Rd

Scores from two systems comparing pairs of recordings of 80 male speakers of German: an automatic speaker recognition system and a formant-based system. Every speaker is compared with himself (same-speaker comparisons, recordings from two sessions) and with every other speaker (different-speaker comparisons). Higher scores mean more similar voices. For calibrating scores into likelihood ratios, computing Cllr and comparing or fusing systems.

Usage

forensic_comparison

Format

A tibble with 3240 rows and 6 columns:

comparison

Comparison ID, C0001 to C3240.

speaker_a, speaker_b

The two speakers, S01 to S80.

same_speaker

"no" or "yes".

score_auto

Score of the automatic system.

score_formant

Score of the formant-based system.

Source

data-raw/forensic_comparison.R

Details

True model: automatic scores are normal with mean 2.5 (SD 1) for same-speaker and -1 (SD 1.3) for different-speaker comparisons; formant scores have means 1 (SD 1) and -0.5 (SD 1.1). Each speaker shifts his scores by a speaker effect (SD 0.4 automatic, 0.3 formant; the mean of the two speakers in different-speaker comparisons). The automatic system discriminates much better: after logistic-regression calibration its Cllr is about 0.25, against about 0.7 for the formant system.

References

Brümmer, N. & du Preez, J. (2006). Application-independent evaluation of speaker detection. Computer Speech and Language, 20(2-3), 230-275. doi:10.1016/j.csl.2005.08.001

Examples

head(forensic_comparison)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   comparison speaker_a speaker_b same_speaker score_auto score_formant
#>   <fct>      <fct>     <fct>     <fct>             <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 C0001      S01       S01       yes               3.42          2.38 
#> 2 C0002      S01       S02       no               -0.201         0.214
#> 3 C0003      S01       S03       no               -0.523        -0.176
#> 4 C0004      S01       S04       no               -1.01         -0.047
#> 5 C0005      S01       S05       no               -3.63          1.07 
#> 6 C0006      S01       S06       no               -0.704         1.48
